title: Scheduled ecosystem scan (reduced form)
intent: Enumerate a versioned source inventory, fetch every source in parallel with bounded retries, meet at exactly one fan-in barrier that window-gates, deduplicates and resolves version disagreements deterministically, and emit one globally ranked digest whose every date and link comes from the committed fixtures. This is the master-plan Pattern 10 reduced to what the runtime actually delivers today; see limitations for everything the full pattern would add.
nonGoals: It is not scheduled. Nothing in this repository runs on a schedule, holds a schedule identity, or takes an overlap lease; every run of this bundle starts because a person invoked a runner. The word 'scheduled' in the title names the master-plan pattern, not a delivered capability.
It does not fetch anything. Every feed result in this bundle comes from the deterministic mock adapter and a committed fixture.
It does not read a clock. The scan window, every publication date and every retrieval date are fixture data; window gating is lexicographic comparison of ISO-8601 strings.
It does not enforce a budget or a rate limit. See policy.budget.enforcement.
It does not enforce a permission or an isolation boundary. See policy.permissions.enforcement.
It does not classify impact or relevance and it does not verify content across sources beyond version-conflict reporting; ranking is by fixture publication date only.
It does not retain partial results when a source fails permanently. See limitations.partialSourceFailureRetention.

graphs.note: Both documents are byte-equivalent after canonicalization, and both language runners assert that against the constructor output before running anything.

constructors.parity: Both constructors produce the same canonical document; the runners assert equality against the committed graph in each language.

fixtures.note: The expected events and the expected digest live in files. The runners and the package tests compare against them; they never restate them inline.

adapters.note: No real provider adapter exists in this repository. See docs/patterns/ecosystem-scan.md#real-provider-setup for what would have to be supplied.

tests.crossLanguage: Both runners compare against the same fixtures/expected-events.json and fixtures/expected-run.json; agreement between the lanes is what the shared files enforce. The Python constructor is additionally tested by python/tests/test_patterns_ecosystem_scan.py.
tests.note: There is no automated packed-install test for this bundle. CI runs all four example runners as subprocesses via `pnpm check:pattern-runners` and validates this manifest via `pnpm check:patterns`.

budget.note: These numbers are documentation, not a control. No runtime component in this repository reads or enforces a token, money, time or rate budget; the master-plan 'bounded rate/cost' requirement is therefore NOT delivered. The only numbers that actually bind a run are the Graph IR policies (maxConcurrency, maxFanOut, maxTotalAttempts) and each fetch node's retry.maxAttempts, which the scheduler does enforce.

modelRouting.declared: One mock adapter per source, selected by source key.
modelRouting.note: Routing here is executor wiring in the example, not a runtime policy object.

permissions.note: There is no isolation provider, so nothing enforces any of this. The master-plan 'per-source privacy/network limits' are therefore NOT delivered. The reason the runs perform no network access is that the code contains no network call and the mock adapter cannot make one — not that a sandbox refused it.

approval.note: This pattern has no human approval step. No approval provider exists.

redaction.declared: Durable payload protection is configured and mandatory; every authoritative value reaches the journal as a protected reference under the default capture policy.
redaction.enforcedBy: durable payload protection; a durable run without it fails closed with PAYLOAD_PROTECTION_REQUIRED before the first event and the first executor call
redaction.note: Both runners assert the fail-closed path.

retention.declared: In-memory journal and payload store for the examples; nothing is written to disk. The master-plan 'retained last-success metadata' between scans is NOT delivered — nothing survives the process.

retry.where: resume.mjs / resume.py, scenario A — GE_ADAPTER_RATE_LIMITED injected on attempt 1 of fetch-registry

crashAndResume.where: resume.mjs / resume.py, scenario B — the journal commits and then loses the process; the resumed run never re-invokes the committed fetch

replay.where: resume.mjs / resume.py — resuming an already terminal run returns the recorded result with zero new events and zero executor calls

failClosedWithoutProtection.where: resume.mjs / resume.py — PAYLOAD_PROTECTION_REQUIRED, zero executor calls

timeout.reason: A deterministic timeout demonstration would need a controllable clock in the run path; this bundle reads no clock at all, by design.

cancellation.reason: Cancellation during ranking is a listed Pattern 10 negative case. It is not demonstrated here.

fork.reason: Replay/fork of a durable run is not exercised by this bundle.

duplicateSyndication.where: fixtures/sources.json — item-cli-release is reported by both the registry and the releases source with the same version; the digest folds it into one entry with two sightings and both sources listed.

versionConflict.where: fixtures/sources.json — item-core-release is version 2.1.0 in the registry source and 2.0.0 in the releases source; normalize resolves it deterministically (highest-version-wins, winner's date and link) and reports both positions in versionConflicts instead of hiding the disagreement.

outOfWindowDate.where: fixtures/sources.json — item-advisory-2025-104 is published before the scan window and is dropped with reason published-outside-scan-window; the drop is in the committed digest, not silent.

scheduleOverlap.reason: There is no schedule identity and no overlap lease. Two concurrent invocations against one shared journal are not fenced by anything in this repository; the master-plan overlap-lease requirement is unimplemented.

partialSourceFailureRetention.reason: The normalize node is a static all-success barrier. If one source fails permanently the barrier is never satisfied and no digest is produced. Retaining partial sources needs quorum or settled barrier behaviour, which is capability-gated and not implemented.

diagrams.traceVisualization: Both runners emit an event-order trace showing the three fetch lanes overlapping and the barrier waiting. The scale is the journal sequence number, not wall-clock time.

limitations.noSchedule: There is no scheduler, no schedule identity and no scheduled-run provenance. The 'scheduled' in the pattern title is aspiration inherited from the master plan; every run here is started by hand.
limitations.noOverlapLease: Nothing fences two concurrent runs. The in-run overlap that IS proven (the promise gate / asyncio.Barrier across the three fetch lanes) is parallelism inside one run, not schedule-overlap protection between runs.
limitations.rankingBarrierIsAllSuccess: The normalize barrier is the static {"condition": "all"} join, not an integrated barrier policy. Quorum, deadline and late-source behaviour do not exist; a permanently failed source yields no digest at all.
limitations.noRealProvider: Nothing in this bundle has ever contacted a feed or a provider. There is no provider client in this repository.
limitations.budgetsAreDocumentation: See policy.budget.enforcement: none. There is no rate limiting and no cost bound beyond the scheduler's attempt policies.
limitations.noImpactClassification: The master-plan impact/relevance classification and cross-source content verification are not implemented; ranking is by fixture publication date with itemId tie-break, and version conflicts are reported, not adjudicated.
limitations.noRetainedLastSuccess: No last-success metadata survives between runs; the journal and payload store are in-memory and vanish with the process.
limitations.datesAreFixtureData: Every date in the digest is committed fixture data compared lexicographically. No clock is read, which also means no defence against a source reporting a plausible-but-wrong date beyond the window gate.
limitations.noObservabilityBackend: There is no metrics or tracing backend. The observability queries in the launch guide are journal projections, not queries against a running system.
limitations.noSupportBundleTool: There is no support-bundle command. The launch guide documents what to collect by hand.
limitations.noIndependentReview: This bundle has not been independently reviewed.
limitations.packedInstallNotTested: No CI job runs the runners from packed artifacts; they run from the workspace build.
